title: The seven archons of the Ophite diagram
source_text: Εἶθ᾿ ἑξῆς ἐπαναλαμβάνει τὰ περὶ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀρχόντων δαιμόνων, μηδαμῶς μὲν ὑπὸ Χριστιανῶν ὀνομαζομένων οἶμαι δ᾿ ὑπὸ Ὀφιανῶν παραλαμβανομένων. καὶ εὕρομέν γε ἐν ᾧ καὶ ἡμεῖς δι᾿ ἐκείνους ἐκτησάμεθα διαγράμματι τὴν τάξιν ὁμοίως ἐκκειμένην οἷς ὁ Κέλσος ἐξέθετο. ὁ μὲν οὖν Κέλσος ἔλεγε τὸν πρῶτον ἰδέᾳ λέοντος μεμορφωμένον, οὐκ ἐκθέμενος, τίνα αὐτὸν ὀνομάζουσιν οἱ ἀληθῶς δυσσεβέστατοι· ἡμεῖς δὲ εὕρομεν ὅτι τὸν ἐν ταῖς ἱεραῖς γραφαῖς εὐφημούμενον ἄγγελον τοῦ δημιουργοῦ, τοῦτον τὸ μιαρὸν ἐκεῖνο διάγραμμα ἔλεγεν εἶναι Μιχαὴλ τὸν λεοντοειδῆ. πάλιν τ᾿ αὖ μὲν Κέλσος ἔφασκε τὸν ἑξῆς καὶ δεύτερον εἶναι ταῦρον· ὃ δ᾿ εἴχομεν διάγραμμα τὸν Σουριὴλ ἔλεγεν εἶναι τὸν ταυροειδῆ. εἶτα ὁ μὲν Κέλσος τρίτον ἀμφίβιόν τινα καὶ φρικῶδες ἐπισυρίζοντα· τὸ δὲ διάγραμμα τρίτον Ῥαφαὴλ ἔλεγεν εἶναι δρακοντοειδῆ. πάλιν τε αὖ ὁ μὲν Κέλσος τὸν τέταρτον ἀετοῦ ἔφασκεν ἔχειν μορφήν· τὸ δὲ διάγραμμα Γαβριὴλ ἔλεγεν εἶναι τὸν ἀετοειδῆ. εἶθ᾿ μὲν Κέλσος τὸν πέμπτον ἔφασκεν εἶναι ἄρκου πρόσωπον ἔχοντα· τὸ δὲ διάγραμμα τὸν Θαυθαβαὼθ ἔφασκεν εἶναι τὸν ἀρκοειδῆ. εἶθ᾿ ὁ μὲν Κέλσος τὸν ἕκτον κυνὸς πρόσωπον ἔλεγεν ἱστορεῖσθαι ἔχειν παρ᾿ ἐκείνοις· τὸ δὲ διάγραμμα ἔφασκεν εἶναι αὐτὸν Ἐραθαώθ. εἶθ᾿ ὁ μὲν Κέλσος τὸν ἕβδομον ἔφασκεν ὄνου ἔχειν πρόσωπον, καὶ ὀνομάζεσθαι αὐτὸν Θαφαβαὼθ ἢ Ὀνοήλ· ἡμεῖς δ᾿ ἐν τῷ διαγράμματι εὕρομεν ὅτι οὗτος καλεῖται Ὀνοὴλ ἢ Θαρθαραὼθ, ὀνοειδής τις τυγχάνων. ἔδοξε δὲ καὶ ἡμῖν ἀκριβῶς ἐκθέσθαι τὰ τοιαῦτα, ἵνα μὴ δοκῶμεν ἀγνοεῖν ἃ Κέλσος ἐπηγγέλλετο εἰδέναι· ἀλλὰ καὶ παραστήσωμεν ἀκριβέστερον ἐκείνου αὐτὰ ἐγνωκότες οἱ Χριστιανοὶ, ὡς οὐ Χριστιανῶν λόγους ἀλλὰ πάντῃ ἀλλοτρίων σωτηρίας καὶ οὐδαμῶς ἐπιγραφομένων Ἰησοῦν ἢ σωτῆρα ἢ θεὸν ἢ διδάσκαλον ἢ υἱὸν θεοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: Then next he takes up again (ἐπαναλαμβάνει) the things about the seven ruling demons (ἑπτὰ ἀρχόντων δαιμόνων), in no way named by Christians, but, I think (οἶμαι), received (παραλαμβανομένων) by the Ophians (Ὀφιανῶν). And we found, in the diagram (διάγραμμα) which we too acquired on their account (δι᾿ ἐκείνους), the order (τάξιν) set out likewise to what Celsus set out. Celsus said the first was shaped in the form (ἰδέᾳ) of a lion (λέοντος μεμορφωμένον), not setting out what the truly most impious (δυσσεβέστατοι) call him; but we found that the angel of the Creator (ἄγγελον τοῦ δημιουργοῦ) spoken well of (εὐφημούμενον) in the holy Scriptures, this one that foul (μιαρόν) diagram said was Michael the lion-shaped (λεοντοειδῆ). Again Celsus said the next and second was a bull; the diagram we had said Suriel was the bull-shaped (ταυροειδῆ). Then Celsus: a third, amphibious (ἀμφίβιον), hissing frightfully (φρικῶδες ἐπισυρίζοντα); the diagram said the third was Raphael, serpent-shaped (δρακοντοειδῆ). Again Celsus said the fourth had the form of an eagle; the diagram said Gabriel was the eagle-shaped (ἀετοειδῆ). Then Celsus said the fifth had a bear's face (ἄρκου πρόσωπον); the diagram said Thauthabaoth was the bear-shaped. Then Celsus said the sixth is reported (ἱστορεῖσθαι) among them to have a dog's face; the diagram said he was Erathaoth. Then Celsus said the seventh had an ass's face and was named Thaphabaoth or Onoel; we found in the diagram that this one is called Onoel or Thartharaoth, being ass-shaped (ὀνοειδής). It seemed good to us too to set out such things exactly (ἀκριβῶς), that we may not seem ignorant of what Celsus professed (ἐπηγγέλλετο) to know; but also that we Christians may show (παραστήσωμεν) that we have known them more exactly than he, as words not of Christians but of people wholly alien to salvation (ἀλλοτρίων σωτηρίας) and in no way inscribing themselves under (ἐπιγραφομένων) Jesus or Saviour or God or Teacher or Son of God.
pass_b_english: Next he takes up again what he said about the seven ruling demons, who are never named by Christians but are, I think, accepted by the Ophites. And indeed, in the diagram that we ourselves obtained because of them, we found the order set out just as Celsus set it out. Celsus said that the first is formed in the shape of a lion, without stating what name these truly most impious people give him. But we found that that foul diagram said the lion-shaped one was Michael, the angel of the Creator who is honoured in the holy Scriptures. Again, Celsus said that the next one, the second, is a bull; the diagram we had said that Suriel is the bull-shaped one. Then Celsus spoke of a third, an amphibious creature that hisses horribly; the diagram said that the third is Raphael, the serpent-shaped. Again, Celsus said that the fourth has the form of an eagle; the diagram said that Gabriel is the eagle-shaped one. Then Celsus said that the fifth has the face of a bear; the diagram said that Thauthabaoth is the bear-shaped one. Then Celsus said that among them the sixth is described as having the face of a dog; the diagram said that he is Erathaoth. Then Celsus said that the seventh has the face of an ass and is named Thaphabaoth or Onoel; but we found in the diagram that he is called Onoel or Thartharaoth, and that he has the shape of an ass.

We too decided to set out such things exactly, so that we may not seem ignorant of what Celsus professed to know, and also so that we Christians may show that we know these things more exactly than he does, and know them as the words not of Christians but of people wholly estranged from salvation, who in no way call themselves by the name of Jesus, or of Saviour, or God, or Teacher, or Son of God.

choices.choice: Ὀφιανοί rendered ‘Ophites’, the usual English name of the serpent sect. δημιουργός here is Origen’s own word for the Creator God (contrast the Gnostic usage in 6.35), so capitalised ‘Creator’. Michael, honoured in Scripture (Daniel 10:13, 21; 12:1; Jude 9; Revelation 12:7), is not a quotation or a verse allusion, so no inline citation. δρακοντοειδής rendered ‘serpent-shaped’ (δράκων = serpent/dragon), kept consistent in 6.33 and 6.37. Spellings of the barbarous names follow the copy-text as printed: Suriel, Thauthabaoth, Erathaoth, Thaphabaoth/Onoel (Celsus), Onoel/Thartharaoth (diagram); the forms vary in the manuscripts and are not normalised. εἶθ᾿ μὲν Κέλσος (article missing in the staged text) read as εἶθ᾿ ὁ μὲν Κέλσος. ἐπιγραφομένων (‘enrol under, claim as title’) rendered ‘claim the name of’.
Michael sentence: dropped added 'very', 'that foul diagram' for ἐκεῖνο, past tense kept
ἐπιγραφομένων: 'call themselves by the name of' (avoids 'claim the name of God' misreading)

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; the English is from the Greek.
